main_statement.headline_choice: Two headlines. The comparator (only Lean target) is the CH obstruction (240-CH Thm 1.1). The higher-profile claim, Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in ZFC (240-EC Thm main:uniform), is NOT formalized.

CH.latex: Assume the continuum hypothesis. There is an abstract elementary class K in a countable finitary relational language such that (i) LS(K)=\aleph_0; (ii) K has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality \beth_{\omega_2}=H(K); (iii) putting \Lambda=\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}, the class K is categorical in every cardinal \mu\ge\Lambda. In particular, \lambda=\Lambda^+>H(K) is a categoricity cardinal from which downward transfer to H(K) fails.
CH.paraphrase: Under CH, the prescribed-threshold form of Shelah's conjecture (categoricity in some lambda >= H(K)=beth_{(2^LS)^+} implies categoricity in all mu >= H(K)) fails: an explicit AEC with LS=aleph_0 has two models at beth_{omega_2}=H(K) yet is categorical from beth_{(2^{aleph_1})^+} on. Cor cor:consistency: if ZFC is consistent, the prescribed-threshold statement is not a ZFC theorem (via Godel's L).

comparator.theorem: OAI.CHObstruction.main (hCH : CH) : exists (L : N -> Type), Countable (Sigma n, L n) and exists K : ClassData L, K.IsAEC and K.HasLSNumber aleph0 and endpoint = hanf aleph0 and K.TwoModels endpoint and forall mu, tailThreshold <= mu -> K.Categorical mu
comparator.model: RelModel L = ZFSet carrier + Prop-valued n-ary relations (relational, finitary, language L : N -> Type 0). IsAEC: strong => objects; refl/antisymm/trans; strong => induced substructure; iso invariance of objects and of strong pairs; coherence; chain_union for every nonzero ordinal gamma (union exists, members strong, smoothness); downward LS. LSBound theta includes aleph0 <= theta and |language| <= theta; HasLSNumber = least LS bound. Categorical includes existence. CH := 2^aleph0 = aleph_1; hanf k = beth((2^k)^+ .ord); endpoint = beth(omega_2); tailThreshold = beth((2^{aleph_1})^+ .ord).

CH.match_check: Comparator definitions (RelModel..tailThreshold) are textually identical (diff -w) to lean/OAI/ModelTheory/Categoricity/Model.lean. Statement matches paper Thm 1.1 (i)-(iii) exactly, including the lower endpoint Lambda of the tail and existence in 'categorical'. 'endpoint = hanf aleph0' is the CH identity beth_{omega_2}=beth_{(2^aleph0)^+}. AEC axioms are the standard Grossberg/Shelah ones (chains of arbitrary ordinal length, smoothness, coherence, LS with language-size bound). No loophole found: models are arbitrary set-sized relational structures, the language is countable, isomorphism is the usual one.
CH.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: Thm 1.1 (i)-(iii) and sibling prescribed_transfer_fails (Main.lean:253, categorical at succ tailThreshold but not at hanf aleph0). Not formalized: Cor cor:consistency (relative consistency via Godel's L; metamathematical), Prop prop:no-amalgamation (failure of JEP/AP), Sec 7 booleanization (dense-cosieve obstruction to Booleanizing the canonical point in Espindola2023Spectra Thm 4.1). lean/docs/240.md confirms.
CH.note_for_comparator: Compile status pending (orchestrator). Text-level trust surface clean.

EC.latex: For every infinite cardinal \lambda there is a cardinal \mu(\lambda)\ge\lambda such that for every AEC K with LS(K)\le\lambda: (\exists\kappa\ge\mu(\lambda) K categorical in \kappa) \Rightarrow (\forall\kappa'\ge\mu(\lambda) K categorical in \kappa'). Qualitative form: an AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail.
EC.paraphrase: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for arbitrary AECs, in ZFC, with no amalgamation/JEP/tameness/large-cardinal/WGCH hypotheses and arbitrary (also singular) starting cardinal. Threshold existential, not explicit; compatible with the CH obstruction because mu(lambda) may exceed H(K).
EC.formalized_vs_claimed: Entire manuscript unformalized; it is a claim resting only on an unrefereed 9.5k-line paper.
EC.priority_note: Espindola (arXiv 1906.09169 v7, 2022) already claims a ZFC proof of the same conjecture; the EC paper cites it as a 'separate public claim' and says none of its interfaces is imported (EC:01-introduction.tex:192-198). Shelah-Vasey JEMS 2024 prove it under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, or WGCH + amalgamation.

eureka_candidates.for: Removes the kappa^theta=kappa / cofinality hypotheses that blocked Shelah's Chapter IV route (gap noted by Boney-Vasey 2015). The device (two categoricity sizes with identical profile; theta^+ rounds of an increasing chain of mu-models that push each tuple of an aligned small submodel out of the orbit reaching p; union of aligned small models must contain p) appears nowhere in the goal and no near neighbour was found. Every later section depends on symmetric strong-map classes.
eureka_candidates.against: Ingredients are classical: EM models over homogeneous orders (Shelah IV.5.1), orbit counting, pigeonhole over a set of profiles. The 'push along the arrow relation until it cannot return' is a familiar maximality/elimination idea. Unformalized; correctness unaudited by experts.

concerns: EC is unreviewed and unformalized; it claims to settle a central open problem of AEC theory. Espindola's earlier claimed ZFC proof (arXiv 1906.09169) has not, to our knowledge, been accepted as settling the conjecture; the companion CH paper itself exhibits a failing step in Espindola2023Spectra.

EC relies on dozens of 'sufficiently closed level' refinements; Sec 13's single common level for all finite depths (majorant Phi over a fixed finite register, G_omega) is the most delicate point: every bound request must be definable and totalized uniformly in the descriptor, and the descriptor set must be fixed before the hypothetical Vaughtian pair is chosen (EC addresses this in Lemma geom:anchored-type and Thm close:common-levels, but it is the classic place for a hidden class-quantification error).

EC Sections 8-9, 11-12 (chain closure of marked pairs, exact boundary lifting, geometric classification) were only partly read; correctness of the return-tree argument depends on lower-dimensional completion and on the orbit bound over parameters (Lemma calc:parameter-orbits) holding at the needed levels.
CH 06-booleanization (topos obstruction) is not formalized; its claim about the precise step of Espindola2023Spectra Thm 4.1 was not checked against that preprint.
CH cor:consistency is a metamathematical statement; only its ZFC+CH core is formalized.
If the Lean build fails or needs extra axioms, CH reduces to a 2.5k-line unrefereed paper (but it is short and checked here by hand).
